messages:
anna: heads up — p99 jumped ~2.3x on nightly bench run for attn-kernel on the 2k-seq workload. likely regression after yesterday's kernel selection changes. attaching quick summary below.

jason: ugh. saw similar noise earlier. any kernel-fallback logs? or is this pure perf delta?

anna: logs show intermittent fallback to generic-kernel at the same time p99 spikes. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:14:12Z] REQUEST id=xyz kernel=optim_fused -> fallback=generic_kernel reason=missing_optimized_kernel
[2026-03-18T02:14:12Z] LATENCY p50=12ms p95=28ms p99=320ms p999=610ms
```

deepak: two quick hypotheses: (1) selection policy misclassifying sequence-length bucket causing non-matching kernel lookup, (2) nondeterministic sampling in bench harness — some runs include rare long-context prompts causing tail.

lia: for triage we should pin the kernel map and run a minimal repro harness: deterministic seed, single client connection, fixed batch size. example command: 
```
KERNEL_MAP=pin ./tools/run_bench --model llama-2-7b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --seed 42 --warmup 200 --iters 2000 --pin-kernel optim_fused
```
Also enable runtime debug: RUNTIME_LOG=kernel_selection,kv_cache,perf ./tools/run_bench ...

sarah: uploaded the CI job artifacts here: https://ci.internal/reports/1954320999/ — includes perf traces + flamegraphs. quick grep shows repeated 'kernel not found' during the window.

ci-bot: Job #1954320999 finished. Artifacts: /artifacts/1954320999/bench-output.tar.gz (size: 12MB).

anna: plan: (1) reproduce locally with lia's pinned command, (2) run with LD_PRELOAD=libnuma to rule out numa scheduling noise, (3) collect perf counters (+context-switch) and nvprof on repro, (4) if repro, bisect the kernel-selection matrix change.

jason: add one more: compare p99 measured at request exit vs. token-emission. if KV cache miss is triggering heavy work on first token, you'll see 1st-token tail but steady thereafter.

deepak: note on harness noise — we recently switched sampler to 'dynamic-mix' which can occasionally pick a 4k example for the 2k-suite due to rounding in the selector. I can revert in a branch and run A/B to confirm.

lia: also try isolating GPU power management: sudo nvidia-smi -pm 1; sudo nvidia-smi -pl 300. some machines showed clock-throttling correlated with long tails.

sarah: small reproducible trace attached in artifacts: `bench-output/trace_20260318_02.tar.gz` — contains kernel-selection debug logs and the per-request latency histogram csv. p99 rows: 310ms, 305ms, 315ms during the event window.

anna: ok I'll run the pinned-kernel + dynamic-sampler-off combo on one of the repro hosts and post results in ~90m. if we can reproduce, we should create an RFC follow-up: kernel-selection invariant and a defensive-mode to avoid fallbacks for hot routes.

jason: short-term mitigation: bump canary threshold to prefer compatible kernels for short sequences until we fix selection logic. but only if we measure no correctness regressions.

deepak: agreement on correctness check: add golden-output diff for 20 deterministic prompts and fail if there's mismatch > token-error-threshold. that will catch accidentally switching to incompatible kernel.

lia: I ran a quick local with pin + seed 42: no fallback and stable p99=14ms. will push the run log in ~20m so we can compare host configs.

sarah: FYI the CI host that saw the spike had older CUDA driver (510.x) vs repro hosts (530.x). could be a driver/kernel combo bug. adding to hypothesis matrix.

anna: TL;DR checklist for triage run — deterministic inputs, pin kernel, disable dynamic sampler, warmup tokens >= 200, isolate concurrency, force GPU pm/perf settings, collect perf+nvprof, compare driver versions, golden-output diffs. I'll post the reproducible trace if I can get one. :eyes:

jason: thanks. if you find a repro I'll start a bisect on the kernel-selection commit range. otherwise we'll roll back the selection change behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:
